newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices seen firming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices seen firming.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices firmed early Monday, tracking gains in the underlying NYMEX heating oil contract as trade opened for the week, traders said.
Diesel basis was seen firming on the week on spot agricultural demand and shipping delays on the regional Explorer pipeline system announced last week, traders said.
"With the delayed shipments, people are going to have to cover for any incremental needs," one trader active in the Group Three market said.

Maintenance and a heavy slate of distillate liftings last week pushed back shipments on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system by five days. The pipeline system expected shipments to be back on its routine schedule by late May.
Midwest spot prices were tracking a 0.50 cent a gallon rise in NYMEX May heating oil and nearly 0.40 cent a gallon drop in front-month unleaded in morning trade.
Low sulphur diesel remained 7.25/7.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Group Three and 1.25/1.50 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
High sulphur also was unchanged at 6.75/7.0 cents over the print in Group Three and 0.75/1.0 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline differentials opened the week unchanged at bids 1.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX May unleaded in Group Three and 1.0 cent under the print in Chicago, traders said.
